question: What are the three parts of Canada’s Parliament?
generated_answer: the Parliament of Canada is made up of three parts: the Sovereign, the Senate, and the House of Commons. You will find more information about the Senate and the House of Commons in the following sections. The Sovereign is the person who represents Canada at home and abroad. The Sovereign is not a member of the Parliament of Canada. The Sovereign is represented by the Governor General, who is appointed by the Sovereign on the advice of the Prime Minister of Canada. The Sovereign’s role is to give assent to bills passed by the Senate and the House of Commons, which makes them laws. The Senate is the upper house of the Parliament of Canada. It is made up of 105 Senators who are appointed by the Governor General on the advice of the Prime Minister. Senators represent the provinces and territories of Canada. The Senate has the power to review and amend bills passed by the House of Commons, and to propose new laws. The House of Commons is the lower house of the Parliament of Canada. It is made up of 338 Members of Parliament (MPs) who are elected by the people of Canada. MPs represent the people of their ridings (electoral districts). The House of Commons has the power to introduce and pass laws, and to hold the government accountable for its actions.
